rename.from: Crash on gitsigns+linematch before expanding snippet
rename.to: linematch.c crash with gitsigns+linematch before expanding snippet

body:
cc @jwhite510 

@przepompownia if you are able to reproduce this consistently, could you see if https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/23569 fixes it?

With the above init.lua I can reproduce this failure both on master and #23569 (after merge master into).

I see I missed one thing needed for reproduction: the existing signs are relevant. Overriding `init.lua` inside the clone of https://github.com/przepompownia/repro.nvim with the above `init.lua` should be sufficient (I'll modify the original post).

```lua
vim.keymap.set({'i'}, '<A-s>', function ()
  vim.snippet.expand('if $1 then\
\t$0\
end')
end)
```
Similar snippet defined manually like the above does not trigger the failure. Is it possible that the built-in LSP and snippet code generates some special character (such as visualized by `^@`) that exposes the error (and maybe Gitsigns performs some calculations that may be premature)?

I was able to reproduce the crash.
linematch_nbuffers is getting called with a null pointer as one of the text inputs. 

it is given this input through a lua function call:
0x7749723c5359 "vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('UIEnter', {\n  once = true,\n  callback = init,\n})\n"
as a length of 3, which makes sense because I see 3 newline characters in that
and it is given a null char* with an expected length of 36. so when it tries to retrieve a line from that null pointer at any position, it dereferences the null pointer and crashes.

![linematchcrash](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/821427b8-4b61-4c25-b654-81f8bfd60852)

to resolve the crash, I can add in some assert statements to check that the input is not null and actually matches the length specified

not quite sure why linematch is given a null char  pointer with a length of 36.

The call is comings from `vim.diff()`

```
#7  0x000055857a7512df in linematch_nbuffers (diff_blk=0x7f325ebfd840, diff_len=0x7f325ebfd838, ndiffs=2, decisions=0x7f325ebfd830, iwhite=false) at .../src/nvim/linematch.c:356
#8  0x000055857a779e7c in get_linematch_results (lstate=0x7f325f780380, ma=<optimized out>, mb=<optimized out>, start_a=50, count_a=<optimized out>, start_b=51, count_b=15, iwhite=false)
    at .../src/nvim/lua/xdiff.c:77
#9  0x000055857a779f91 in hunk_locations_cb (start_a=<optimized out>, count_a=<optimized out>, start_b=<optimized out>, count_b=<optimized out>, cb_data=<optimized out>) at .../src/nvim/lua/xdiff.c:133
#10 0x000055857a8d1182 in xdl_call_hunk_func (xe=<optimized out>, xscr=<optimized out>, ecb=0x7f325ebfda80, xecfg=0x7f325ebfdaf0) at .../src/xdiff/xdiffi.c:993
#11 0x000055857a8d3dad in xdl_diff

```

So something in that chain is passing a NULL pointer.

body:
I re compiled with https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/30512
and the test case described by [przepompownia](https://github.com/przepompownia) no longer crashed
The current version of #30512 at least protects against the failure.

Are you able to determine why the string has a NUL character? Is it contained in the string that is passed to `vim.diff()`? Is the snippet engine inserting NUL characters?

@MariaSolOs @mfussenegger do either of you know?
